2609.08094.title: CIVI: A Framework for Diagnosing Search Agent Failures in Civic Information
2609.08094.paper_summary: Large Language Models are increasingly deployed in public-sector settings, where incorrect guidance can cause irreversible harm. We introduce CIVI, the first framework for diagnosing search agent failures in civic information. Its benchmark instantiation jointly spans cross-national, interjurisdictional government contexts (federal, state, and local) and functional categories from an internationally adopted United Nations standard. We evaluate ten frontier search agents and find that none matches an attentive human baseline. Alongside accuracy, CIVI measures search invocation rate, selective no-search accuracy, and how often agents cite authoritative government sources. To perform this diagnosis, we introduce ARISE, which decomposes agentic search failures into four mutually exclusive modes, isolated via source-injection ablation. ARISE attributes 72.1% of all observed failures to retrieval-bound causes rather than to gaps in the models' parametric knowledge.
2609.08094.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型越來越多地應用於公共部門環境中，錯誤的指導可能會造成不可逆的傷害。<lb/>我們介紹CIVI，這是第一個用於診斷公民信息搜索代理失敗的框架。<lb/>其基準實例涵蓋了跨國、跨管轄區的政府背景（聯邦、州和地方）以及來自國際認可的聯合國標準的功能類別。<lb/>我們評估了十個前沿搜索代理，發現沒有一個能與專注的人類基準相匹配。<lb/>除了準確性外，CIVI還衡量搜索調用率、選擇性無搜索準確性，以及代理引用權威政府來源的頻率。<lb/>為了進行這一診斷，我們介紹了ARISE，它將代理搜索失敗分解為四種相互排斥的模式，通過源注入消融進行隔離。<lb/>ARISE將72.1%的所有觀察到的失敗歸因於檢索限制的原因，而不是模型參數知識的缺口。
